bib.title: Building a QA agent with LangGraph (ch. 15 of Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action)

question: How do you implement the chapter-14 expert-emulating KG question-answering design as a working LangGraph pipeline with a Streamlit front end?
contributions: A LangGraph pipeline of intent detection, schema extraction, text-to-Cypher, query execution (with retry) and summary generation
A schema provider that turns apoc.meta.schema output into an LLM-friendly schema via a YAML skip list and descriptions
A question-processing generator that streams pipeline events to a Streamlit app
A five-step investigative walkthrough on a crime/ANPR-camera KG

results.claim: Failed Cypher queries are retried through the text-to-Cypher node with the error fed back, up to three attempts.
results.setup: Chapter's post_query_execution dynamic edge; retries counter reset to 0 by schema extraction and incremented after each execution; no evaluation data
results.quote: allows up to three attempts to execute the query
results.note: Code is `if state["retries"] < 3`, which with an increment after each execution gives three executions in total.

results.claim: Only graph and map outputs are summarised; tabular output ends the pipeline without a summary.
results.quote: for tabular results, which are typically self-explanatory, the pipeline can conclude directly

results.claim: The schema provider calls apoc.meta.schema on the whole database without sampling.
A demo investigation shows a selection-aware, five-step workflow; no accuracy or latency figures are reported.
results.setup: Subset crime KG (Crime, ANPRCamera, CameraEvent, Vehicle, Person); qualitative screenshots only
results.quote: Return any ANPR camera node located within 1 km from the selected crime.

results.claim: The authors cite studies saying in-context learning underperforms task-specific adaptation even with the same examples, and propose fine-tuning as a future direction.
results.source: refs [1], [2] in the chapter (not named in the text)
results.quote: Studies have shown that in-context learning, although flexible, consistently underperforms compared to task-specific adaptation approaches [1], [2].

limits: No evaluation: no accuracy, latency, cost or model identity (LLM, temperature) is stated for the pipeline; the chapter is a demonstration only.
The authors call it 'a foundation rather than a turnkey solution' and Streamlit a prototyping tool.
Listing inconsistencies: output_reason vs state key output_type_reason; summary_analisys misspelt; results_error typed list but holds str/None; self.memory never defined in Listing 15.12.
Only neo4j.exceptions.ClientError is caught, so empty results are not retried.
practices: Keep prompt templates, KG notes and few-shot examples in a YAML config separate from code (15.1.2).
Convert the technical schema to a conceptual one with a skip list plus business descriptions, stored in YAML (15.1.3).
Run the pipeline in stream mode and emit typed (type, payload, state) events so frontends can show progress (15.1.6).
Route on query errors with a bounded retry, feeding the failed query and error back (15.1.5).
Ask 'What would an expert do?' when improving the system (15.4).
Collect complaint-like questions and successful reasoning chains to improve examples (15.4.1).
Consider schema enrichment agents and multilayer schemas for large KGs (15.4.2).

terms.definition: an approach that mimics how human experts interact with graph databases
a shared memory space that agents can read from and write to
